run_scope: broad (10 decisions aligned to PRD-v2 FRs + open OIs)
framer_notes: Each decision carries a claude_code_layer_attachment field naming the agent/skill/KB file the decision attaches to — grounding design-cc's authoring per orchestrator instruction. Externally-pre-decided decisions still enumerate options (so design-composer's selection is visible) but mark the recommendation strongly. Confidence calibration per knowledge skill: verified+independent ⇒ 0.8; verified+vendor-only ⇒ 0.5; single_sourced ⇒ 0.5; partially_verified ⇒ 0.65.

decisions.title: OI-A1: Use a companion-file (machine-checkable) prescription extraction path for FR-1 design-realization audits — not NLP-parse of ADR prose
decisions.context: FR-1 (mechanism H3, design-realization audit) requires the architecture auditor to extract authored prescriptions from ADRs and validate the realization. Two paths are on the table: (a) parse the ADR prose with NLP, or (b) read a machine-checkable companion artifact sibling to each ADR. Discovery confirms no *.yaml siblings to ADR-*.md exist in adrs/ today (C-0136), so companion-file is a new convention; NLP-parse path would operate on the canonical ADR prose body protected by ADR-0036 (single canonical location) and ADR-0056 (no carve-outs) (C-0137). External research T-002 surveyed 9 production systems (Nygard ADR, MADR, Archgate, kschlt adr-kit, DECIDER, rvdbreemen adr-kit, ArchUnit, Pact, OpenAPI/Schemathesis/Dredd, Spectral, Terraform Sentinel/OPA) — 9/9 use machine-checkable companion artifacts, and the peer-reviewed counterexample (arXiv 2602.07609) found LLM-based NLP-parse misinterprets 44.57% of the time. T-002 is the strongest cross-source triple in this run. Discovery does not pre-decide (C-0154) but external evidence tilts decisively toward companion-file.
options_summary: Companion-file path (RECOMMENDED — 9/9 surveyed precedent, peer-reviewed NLP failure rate; sibling YAML/JSON spec next to each ADR with machine-checkable predicates)
NLP-parse path (operates on existing canonical ADR prose; no new convention but 44.57% misinterpret rate per arXiv 2602.07609; inherits ADR-0036/ADR-0056 constraints)
Hybrid (NLP-parse used only to surface drafts; companion-file is canonical for audit)
risks: Companion-file establishes a new repo convention — escape hatch needed if authoring-burden NFR is breached
ADR-0036 single-canonical-location and ADR-0056 no-carve-outs constrain how companion-file relates to canonical ADR (companion must not duplicate the decision; only its machine-checkable predicates)
Single-sourced FP claim: C-0239 (arXiv 2602.07609 not externally re-fetched in Critic sweep)
Transferability caveat: T-002's 9 surveyed systems are all code/spec domains, not pipeline-document content

decisions.title: OI-A2: Adopt hybrid (denormalized declaration, centralized body) invariant authoring shape for FR-3 PV-tier cross-file invariants
decisions.context: FR-3 (mechanism H9, PV-tier cross-file invariants) demands a catalog authoring shape. Three options: (a) denormalized (declare invariants at each artifact), (b) centralized (single catalog file, all invariants in one place), (c) hybrid (declare at artifact, body lifted into central catalog and referenced). External research T-004 surveyed 6 systems (Terraform, dbt, OpenAPI, JSON Schema, ArchUnit, Bazel) plus the Shopify Packwerk retrospective. T-004 finds the hybrid pattern is the documented sweet spot across every survey datapoint (C-0367) — and crucially, Shopify Packwerk's 'tried-centralized, walked back' retrospective (C-0350, C-0352, C-0365, C-0366) is the strongest available counterexample to a fully-centralized choice. T-004's recommendation framing (C-0368) is appropriately scoped: hybrid is the default; reserve centralized-only for genuinely reusable invariant bodies. Discovery does not pre-decide.
options_summary: Hybrid: denormalized declaration at artifact, body in central catalog (RECOMMENDED — 6/6 surveyed sweet spot; Shopify Packwerk migration retrospective is strongest counter to full-central)
Denormalized: each artifact declares + defines its invariants in-line (best locality; worst DRY)
Centralized: all invariants in one catalog file, artifacts reference (best DRY; Packwerk-style walkback risk)
risks: Partially-verified claim: C-0366 (Packwerk 'different-teams' framing is T-004 author's gloss, defensible but not in retrospective verbatim)
Transferability caveat: T-004 surveyed code/data/API artifacts, NOT pipeline-document content (T-004 open question 1 acknowledges this directly)
Default-to-hybrid rubric: reserve centralized-only invariant bodies for genuinely reusable predicates; in-line if used once

decisions.title: OI-A3: Scope of auditing-skills reverse-check — extend FR-10 (auditing-subagents rule) or author a separate rule for auditing-skills
decisions.context: FR-10 (mechanism B5) mandates a feature-touch-coverage rule on auditing-subagents (sub-agent file → owning skill family back-reference). The question for OI-A3 is whether the analogous reverse-check should live as a rule in auditing-skills as well, or whether FR-10's scope is sufficient. Externally-undecided: no T-001..T-004 finding speaks to this; the auditing-shared (E-0034) / auditing-mcp (E-0031) / auditing-cc-configs (E-0033) skill family carries its own conventions but Discovery has not surveyed analogous reverse-checks. Low blast radius — the change is one rule file under one skill family.
options_summary: Extend FR-10 scope to cover auditing-skills (one rule, two surfaces)
Author separate rule in auditing-skills/ (separation of concerns)
Defer — only FR-10 ships now; auditing-skills reverse-check added later if the audit gap is observed
risks: Externally undecided — no T-001..T-004 corroborator (Critic single-sourced from Discovery)
Low-blast component decision; reversible — but if deferred, document the deferral in §O posture
Sole supporting claim cluster is internal (C-0123, C-0131); no peer-review or vendor cross-corroboration

decisions.title: OI-A5: Establish Blocks-X marker grammar (period-terminated kebab-case `<stage-slug>-completion`) as a first-class precedent
decisions.context: FR-9 (mechanism B4) requires Blocks-X markers to be emitted from Discovery output and consumed by the gate/validator cluster. Discovery surfaced n=1 prior occurrence of the grammar (devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 precedent, E-0074: 'Blocks <stage-slug>-completion.'). With only one precedent, this is effectively a grammar-establishment decision rather than a reconciliation one. Externally-undecided. Low blast radius (single grammar specification); but downstream consumption by FR-2 conformance, FR-3 PV-tier invariants, and AC-FR-9-* makes the wire format mildly load-bearing.
options_summary: Establish precedent grammar verbatim: 'Blocks <stage-slug>-completion.' (period-terminated kebab-case stage slugs)
Extend grammar: allow multiple slugs ('Blocks <slug>, <slug>-completion.') for multi-stage blocks
Reconcile to YAML-friendly token list (drop the period; lift to structured frontmatter)
risks: n=1 prior occurrence — establishment, not reconciliation; risk of premature lock-in
Downstream consumers (FR-2 conformance schema, AC-FR-9-* assertions) inherit the grammar — change cost rises after FR-2 ships
Externally undecided

decisions.title: OI-A6: Mechanical evaluator for FR-6 trigger conditions 3 and 4 — machine-checkable predicate vs human checkpoint vs hybrid
decisions.context: FR-6 (mechanism B1) makes the agent-roster-impact-matrix mandatory at design time. Trigger conditions 3 and 4 are interpretive ('skill-coverage decision present', 'cross-skill impact'); the mechanical evaluator question is how to enforce them automatically. Externally-undecided — T-003 confirms the W/H/A trifecta content for FR-7 (the adjacent decision) but does not specify a trigger-evaluation algorithm. Options: (a) machine-checkable predicate over Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions section, (b) explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoint at Design Composition gate, (c) hybrid (predicate fires advisory; human ratifies). The hybrid is the lower-risk middle path given the interpretive nature.
options_summary: Machine-checkable predicate over Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions section (deterministic; risks false negatives on interpretive triggers)
Human-in-the-loop checkpoint at Design Composition gate (highest signal; ritual cost)
Hybrid: predicate fires advisory annotation; human ratifies at gate (RECOMMENDED — balances cost and signal)
risks: Externally undecided — no T-001..T-004 corroborator for trigger-evaluation pattern
Trigger 3 and 4 are interpretive; pure-mechanical risks brittle false negatives
Predicate-only path conflicts with FR-7's W/H/A substance-not-presence heuristic (D-0008)

decisions.title: OI-A4 / Contingency Split: Single feature (R1) vs split (R2a design-time / R2b gate-validator) posture
decisions.context: PRD §Contingency Split sets a threshold of 12 cumulative open items; if exceeded, the feature is split into R2a (design-time cluster: FR-1, FR-6, FR-7, FR-8, FR-9, FR-10) and R2b (gate/validator cluster: FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-11). Critic verified (C-0004, C-0145) the codebase researcher's expansive 14-OI count (8 IC + 6 PRD-v2) trips the threshold mechanically — but the orchestrator's currently-open count of 6 (only PRD-v2 OI-A1..OI-A6 unresolved) does not. Discovery recommendation: design-composer must apply the threshold mechanically at Gate 4 (C-0006, verbatim from source). The decision is genuinely ambiguous — both readings have evidence — and belongs to design-composer at Gate 4, NOT to design-cc. The framer surfaces the ambiguity and the mechanism-dependency table (R2a/R2b cluster membership per C-0114/C-0116/C-0125/C-0126/C-0127) as input.
options_summary: R1 single feature (orchestrator's 6-OI count; threshold not tripped)
R2a/R2b split per mechanism-dependency clusters (codebase-researcher's 14-OI count; threshold tripped mechanically)
Apply the threshold mechanically per C-0006 — Gate 4 design-composer decides
risks: Genuine ambiguity in count scope (8+6=14 cumulative vs 6 currently-open) — both readings well-evidenced
Split is one-way: undoing requires re-merging downstream artifacts; high cost
Decision belongs to design-composer at Gate 4, not design-cc — framer surfaces evidence and routes
Mechanism-dependency table verified (C-0114, C-0125, C-0126, C-0127) — clusters are not arbitrary
decisions.claude_code_layer_attachment: N/A — design-composer scope, not design-cc; framer routes for transparency

decisions.title: FR-5: Adopt the four-stage drift-detection pipeline (RFC 8785 JCS normalize → persisted canonical baseline → RFC 6902 JSON-Patch diff with identity-keyed array diff → locally-enumerated severity catalog modeled on oasdiff)
decisions.context: FR-5 (mechanism H8, tool-surface drift detection) requires drift detection over MCP tools/list responses with NFR-4 target of <5% false-positive rate across 50 audits. External research T-001 produced a strong cross-source triple: each of the four stages is grounded in an independent primary (RFC 8785 for JCS normalization, oasdiff's change-fingerprint pattern for baseline-as-bytes, RFC 6902 for diff, oasdiff severity catalog as model). T-001 author argues the crucial FP-suppression move is normalization (step 1) and severity-catalog routing (step 4), not the diff algorithm itself (C-0195) — supported by the openapi-diff Issue #673 cautionary tale. The synthesis composition (oasdiff-style catalog applied to MCP tools/list) is novel but each underlying primitive is well-cited. Open sub-decision: NFR-4 <5% FP target measurement strategy — T-001 surfaces that no surveyed source publishes a quantitative benchmark; C-0201 / C-0202 are single-sourced hypotheses (not measured outcomes).
options_summary: Four-stage pipeline: JCS → baseline-as-bytes → RFC 6902 diff (identity-keyed arrays) → local severity catalog (RECOMMENDED — strong cross-source triple)
Naive object-diff + heuristic severity (rejected — openapi-diff Issue #673 evidence; exceeds 5% FP on stable upstream)
Vendor wrapper (oasdiff direct or Buf protobuf — does not cover MCP tools/list schema)
risks: Single-sourced achievability claim: C-0201 (no primary quantifies <5% FP under these exact conditions; extrapolated mechanism)
Single-sourced warning: C-0202 (50-audit description-polishing/CDN-rewrite scenario hypothetical, not measured)
Composition step (oasdiff-style catalog → MCP tools/list) is single-sourced in T-001 but defensible
Open sub-decision: NFR-4 measurement strategy — recommend pilot run as hypothesis-validation at Phase Validator time

decisions.title: FR-7: Frame the Why/How/Anti-patterns trifecta as substance to apply, not a mandatory artifact ritual — reviewers and authors apply substance-not-presence heuristic
decisions.context: FR-7 (mechanism B3, skill-coverage decisions) requires a structured rationale for each skill-coverage decision. T-003 surveyed 6 platforms (Anthropic Agent Skills, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel) and found cross-platform convergence on three recurring categories: need-justification (Why), scope/lifecycle hygiene (How), anti-pattern defenses (Anti-patterns). The trifecta content is universal community substance (C-0256). The novel move is codifying it as a single mandated artifact authored at design time (C-0257) — no surveyed platform mandates this artifact shape. T-003 explicitly surfaces the anti-ritualism trade-off (line 177). The substance-vs-mandate distinction matters: reviewers and authors apply a substance-not-presence heuristic (the trifecta is satisfied if the substance is present, not because three labelled headings exist).
options_summary: Substance-as-rubric: W/H/A is what reviewers check for; structured artifact optional (RECOMMENDED — preserves substance, avoids ritualism)
Mandate-as-artifact: three labelled headings required; reviewer checks presence (novel per T-003; ritualism risk)
Hybrid: artifact-template provided as default with substance-rubric as the auditable standard
risks: Single-sourced quantitative: C-0293 (BFCL 96%→13-15% cliff cited as directional, not measured threshold)
Mandate-as-artifact is novel — no surveyed platform precedent (anti-ritualism cost)
Substance heuristic is harder to mechanically evaluate — couples back to D-0005

decisions.title: FR-11 §O posture: Place event-triggered / honest-acceptance / concrete-machinery framings in discipline texts where post-ship prose currently exists or is being added
decisions.context: FR-11 (mechanism §O) replaces post-ship-felt-utility framings with three replacement postures: event-triggered (concrete review trigger), honest-acceptance (decision is final), concrete-machinery (mechanism is named). Codebase showed zero 'post-ship' prose in .claude/skills/ and .claude/agents/ today — this is purely additive prescription. The placement decision is which discipline texts get the §O wording: AC-FR-11-c currently enumerates four rows (E-3, A-3, D-5, I-1) but §O.1 register names five (adds E-2) (C-0033, C-0153 partially_verified — 5-row count confirmed directly; 4-row enumeration relies on codebase-analysis report's quotation of PRD AC-FR-11-c without direct PRD re-read). Sub-decision: should AC-FR-11-c be expanded to cover E-2? Discovery routes this to design-composer.
options_summary: Place §O wording on discipline texts identified by §O.1 register five-row set (A-3, D-5, E-2, E-3, I-1)
Place §O wording on AC-FR-11-c four-row set (E-3, A-3, D-5, I-1) — exclude E-2
Expand AC-FR-11-c to five rows (include E-2) and apply uniformly — routes to design-composer
risks: Partially-verified count mismatch: C-0033 (4-row enumeration not re-verified against PRD-v2 directly)
Open question explicitly routed to design-composer (C-0153) — design-cc proposes placement but design-composer ratifies scope
Zero 'post-ship' precedent in .claude/skills/ .claude/agents/ today — purely additive (low collision risk)
decisions.claude_code_layer_attachment: .claude/skills/ and .claude/agents/ (discipline texts; specific files per §O.1 register rows) + Issues/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals/register.md (anchor)

decisions.title: Severity vocabulary reconciliation across FR-1 / FR-4 / FR-5 / FR-9 / FR-10 — three coexisting vocabularies must converge or be explicitly partitioned by audience
decisions.context: Codebase researcher surfaced three coexisting severity vocabularies in the auditor/reviewer/validator surface: (a) auditor BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT (used by review-architecture-auditor, auditing-mcp, auditing-cc-configs, auditing-shared per C-0094/C-0097/C-0098/C-0101); (b) reviewer critical/important/recommended (used by shared-document-reviewer, KB-review-disciplines per C-0095/C-0099); (c) phase-validator blocking/warning/informational (used by test-phase-validator-author per C-0100/C-0103). FR-1/FR-4/FR-5/FR-9/FR-10 all emit findings consumed across these surfaces. Externally-undecided — T-001..T-004 do not address vocabulary reconciliation. Cluster graph: E-0068 (auditor), E-0069 (reviewer), E-0070 (phase-validator) all linked to C-0108 (vocabulary-reconciliation claim). Decision is reconciliation strategy: unify (one vocabulary across all surfaces, requires migration cost), partition (each surface keeps its vocabulary, document mapping table), or canonicalize (pick one as canonical, others map via documented translator).
options_summary: Unify: one vocabulary across auditor + reviewer + validator (highest discipline; highest migration cost)
Partition with mapping table: each surface keeps its vocabulary; explicit translation table maintained
Canonicalize: pick auditor BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT as canonical (most populous; widest in-repo footprint); others map via documented translator (RECOMMENDED middle path)
risks: Externally undecided — no T-001..T-004 corroborator (Critic single-sourced from codebase researcher)
Decision belongs to design-composer (cross-cuts multiple layer agents) — design-cc cannot ratify alone
Unify-option migration touches multiple skill families (auditing-mcp, auditing-subagents, auditing-cc-configs, auditing-shared, KB-review-disciplines) — high coordination cost
Canonicalize-option requires careful translator semantics (BLOCKER → critical → blocking is not strictly monotonic across all dimensions)
decisions.decision_owner: design-composer (cross-cuts layers); design-cc proposes for the cc layer
